skill.name: gpt-image-edit
skill.description: Edit existing images with GPT Image 2 through the RunComfy CLI, with guidance for preservation prompts, text replacement, multi-reference edits, and output sizing.
skill.summary: Use GPT Image 2 on RunComfy for precise image edits and multilingual in-image text changes.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, example URLs, and relative links in documentation. The remaining confirmed risks are expected for this skill: prompts and image URLs are processed by RunComfy, and the RunComfy CLI may store an API token in a hidden user config file.

remediation.issue: Third-party processing of image URLs and prompts
remediation.suggestion: Keep the privacy disclosure prominent and advise users not to submit confidential images unless their RunComfy account and data policies permit it.

remediation.issue: Local API token stored in hidden config file
remediation.suggestion: Continue recommending RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI and document token rotation or logout steps for shared machines.

remediation.issue: Skill relies on a local CLI and npm installation
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to install the RunComfy CLI from the official package source and review commands before running them.

content.user_title: Edit Images with GPT Image 2 on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Image edits often drift from the original subject, layout, or brand details. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured RunComfy prompts for precise GPT Image 2 edits.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use GPT Image 2 edit instead of related image models.
Provides RunComfy CLI commands for single-reference image edits.
Shows prompt patterns for preserving faces, poses, brands, and layout.
Supports guidance for multilingual in-image text replacement.
Documents multi-reference composition with up to 10 image URLs.
Lists expected input fields, size values, and common exit codes.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and access to GPT Image 2.
Input images must be publicly fetchable HTTPS URLs.
Long compound edit requests can cause visual drift and should be split.
It documents CLI usage rather than providing a custom local editor.

use_cases.title: Localize advertisement artwork
use_cases.description: Replace in-image headlines with quoted multilingual text while preserving layout and brand marks.

use_cases.title: Update product or portrait backgrounds
use_cases.description: Change a scene or background while keeping the main subject, face, pose, and product details stable.

use_cases.title: Compose multi-reference concepts
use_cases.description: Combine subject, room, lighting, and style cues from numbered image references in a controlled edit prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Basic preservation edit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one image edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gpt-image-edit to keep the person, pose, and clothing unchanged. Replace the background with a clean studio setting. Use this image URL: [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Replace in-image text
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate or rewrite a headline inside an image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gpt-image-edit to keep the photo, layout, and brand mark unchanged. Replace only the headline with "[TEXT]" in [SCRIPT OR LANGUAGE]. Use this image URL: [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Multi-reference composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gpt-image-edit with image 1 as the subject and image 2 as the environment. Match lighting from image 2 while preserving the subject identity from image 1. URLs: [URL 1], [URL 2].

prompt_templates.title: Advanced layout-safe campaign variant
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce a precise marketing variant with explicit constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gpt-image-edit to preserve the product, logo, camera angle, colors, and spacing. Move the headline from [OLD POSITION] to [NEW POSITION], replace it with "[TEXT]", and keep size auto. Image URL: [URL].

output_examples.input: Edit a portrait so the background becomes a warm gray studio sweep while the face and pose stay unchanged.
output_examples.output: A RunComfy GPT Image 2 edit command with a preservation-first prompt, one image URL, and an output directory.

output_examples.input: Replace an English poster headline with Japanese kana without changing the layout.
output_examples.output: A prompt that quotes the exact Japanese text, names the script, and limits the change to the headline area.

output_examples.input: Place a subject from one reference image into a room from another reference image.
output_examples.output: A numbered multi-reference prompt that assigns identity to image 1 and lighting and room cues to image 2.

best_practices: Start prompts with the elements that must remain unchanged.
Quote exact replacement text and name the language or script.
Use size auto unless the edit intentionally changes the frame.
anti_patterns: Do not combine many unrelated edits in one prompt.
Do not submit confidential images unless third-party processing is approved.
Do not use vague text replacement instructions when exact characters are required.

faq.question: Does this skill edit images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI to call GPT Image 2 through the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: What image inputs does it support?
faq.answer: It documents up to 10 publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs, with the first image as the primary reference.

faq.question: Can it replace text inside an image?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill gives prompt patterns for exact quoted text replacement in multiple scripts.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I avoid submitting?
faq.answer: Avoid confidential images, private URLs, or regulated content unless your organization approves RunComfy processing.

faq.question: Why does it mention other image models?
faq.answer: It helps users choose GPT Image Edit when preservation, text replacement, or multi-reference edits are the best fit.
